clinicalPearls: A fulminant herpesvirus retinitis, most often caused by varicella-zoster virus or herpes simplex virus, occurring in immunocompetent as well as immunocompromised people
Presents with a painful red eye, floaters and reducing vision, with prominent anterior and vitreous inflammation
The hallmark is one or more discrete peripheral areas of full-thickness retinal necrosis that spread circumferentially and coalesce
An occlusive retinal arteritis is characteristic and helps distinguish it from other retinitides
Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment from multiple necrotic breaks is the leading cause of severe visual loss
Prompt systemic antiviral therapy, sometimes with intravitreal antiviral supplementation, is central to management
The fellow eye is at risk, so timely diagnosis and treatment aim to protect both eyes
reference.pathophysiology: Reactivation or primary infection with varicella-zoster or herpes simplex virus produces a necrotising retinitis with an occlusive vasculitis of the retinal arterioles. Viral replication in the outer and inner retina causes rapidly enlarging areas of full-thickness necrosis, while the accompanying vasculitis compounds ischaemic damage. As the inflammation resolves the necrotic retina becomes atrophic and develops multiple breaks at the junction of necrotic and healthy retina, predisposing to rhegmatogenous detachment; vitreous inflammation and traction add to the detachment risk.
additionalDifferentials: Behcet or other non-infective occlusive retinal vasculitis
additionalInvestigations: Aqueous or vitreous sampling for viral PCR (HSV, VZV, CMV)
Dilated fundus examination documenting the extent of necrosis and vasculitis
Serology and workup to exclude syphilis, tuberculosis and toxoplasma mimics
Assessment of immune status where relevant
Wide-field imaging and optical coherence tomography to monitor progression
redFlags: Rapidly enlarging retinitis threatening the macula or optic nerve
Involvement or symptoms in the fellow eye
Optic neuropathy with acute severe visual loss
reference.prognosis: Visual outcome is guarded, dominated by the high rate of retinal detachment and by optic nerve or macular involvement; early antiviral treatment reduces fellow-eye disease and severe complications.
pitfalls: Mistaking early ARN for idiopathic anterior uveitis and delaying antiviral therapy
Attributing the picture to CMV retinitis, which is indolent with little vitritis
Failing to anticipate and monitor for retinal detachment
references: American Uveitis Society diagnostic criteria for acute retinal necrosis
